title: Dr. Sue Morter: "The Energetic Architecture of Awakening"
description:

title: Terri Cole: “Healing the Worthiness Wound”
description:
Terri Cole calls it an invisible wound: the imprint left when a daughter never receives protection, presence, or emotional attunement from her father. This week, Tami Simon talks with Terri Cole—Sounds True's own Boundary Boss—about her new book, Father Wound, and why even women with loving fathers can carry this wound without ever naming it.Terri Cole, MSW, LCSW, is a licensed psychotherapist, relationship expert, and best-selling author who has spent nearly three decades helping people break dysfunctional patterns and build healthier relationships with themselves and others. With Sounds True, she is the author of the trilogy that began with Boundary Boss and continued with Too Much: A Guide to Breaking the Cycle of High-Functioning Codependency. Her newest book, Father Wound: Break Unhealthy Patterns to Reclaim Your Worth and Power, examines what happens when a father or father figure is absent, abusive, immature, or simply not emotionally attuned—and why daughters of patriarchy carry a version of this wound no matter what kind of father they had.In this conversation, Tami and Terri explore:- How to recognize a father wound even when "my father wasn't that bad"- Why Terri defines the father wound as, at its root, a worthiness wound- The difference between self-parenting and re-parenting, and what healing your inner child looks like in daily decisions- The "father wound trance": how old patterns resurface in adult relationships, and how to work with transference instead of being run by it- Mourning the Dream, Terri's exercise for grieving the father you wished you'd had- Why healing this wound personally is tied to healing patriarchy at a collective, societal levelWho this episode is for: anyone doing inner child work, anyone who keeps finding themselves in the same relationship pattern and wondering why, and anyone ready to ask whether their sense of worth was shaped long before they had any say in it.Listen now, and start reclaiming your worth. →This interview originally aired on Sounds True One, where you can enjoy early, ad-free access to episodes of Insights at the Edge: https://join.soundstrue.com/

title: Diane Poole Heller: "The Surprising Superpowers of Insecure Attachment"
description:
What if the parts of you that feel the most "broken" in relationships are actually superpowers in disguise? Tami Simon speaks with psychologist and attachment expert Dr. Diane Poole Heller about her new book, The Attachment Workbook, and why insecure attachment patterns aren't flaws to fix, but adaptive responses to understand—and heal.Dr. Diane Poole Heller is an internationally recognized expert, author, and speaker specializing in adult attachment theory and trauma resolution. A former senior faculty member for Somatic Experiencing International, she studied for decades alongside trauma pioneer Dr. Peter Levine before developing DARE (Dynamic Attachment Re-patterning Experience), a somatic framework for healing insecure attachment. She is the author of The Power of Attachment and, most recently, The Attachment Workbook: Practical Exercises to Understand Your Patterns, Strengthen Connection, and Build Secure Relationships, part of Sounds True's Inner Workbook series.In this conversation, Tami and Diane explore:Why secure attachment is biological—something we're all wired for, not something only some people getThe hidden "superpowers" of avoidant, ambivalent, and disorganized attachment stylesHow attachment wounds get physically trapped in the nervous system, and how the body completes what it couldn't finishThe near-death experience that redirected Diane's life's work toward love and connectionWhy healing attachment doesn't require a partner, and how your relationship with yourself can be the starting pointThe research-backed power of repair in relationships, and why learning to apologize well may matter more than never rupturing at allPractical visualization exercises from The Attachment Workbook, including inviting in an imagined protector and healing the "attachment gaze"This episode is for anyone who has wondered why connection feels so hard—whether you're a therapist, a partner, a parent, or simply someone ready to understand your own relational patterns with more compassion.Listen now to discover why secure attachment isn't a fixed trait—it's a skill, and it's never too late to learn it.This interview originally aired on Sounds True One, where you can enjoy early, ad-free access to episodes of Insights at the Edge: https://join.soundstrue.com/

Tami and Adreanna discuss what it means to be "worthy" and why challenges are actually invitations to practice. With Sounds True, he released the audio program Leap First: Creating Work That Matters. In this episode of Insights at the Edge, Tami Simon and Seth discuss the concept of resistance and how it must be sought out in any effective pursuit of art. They also talk about the contemporary "connection economy" and how there is no guarantee that one can make a living through genuine self-expression—but also how one should do so anyway. Finally, they spoke on the necessity of taking leaps and Seth’s concept of living a life of faith. (62 minutes)

Tami's Takeaway: Seth Godin looks at a picture every day that depicts a person triumphantly jumping off of a third story building onto a street below. The caption: "Leap into the Void." Seth leaps every day and inspires others to do the same. He teaches us not to wait to be discovered—for someone to choose us to come forward. Instead, we take the leap and "pick ourselves," engaging in the creative act of being vulnerable, making art, and expressing ourselves. And whether 10 people notice or 10 million, we have the deep satisfaction of living courageously and pouring out our creative souls in ways that matter.
